# BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization — facts

> Source-anchored units about BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization: 20 across 8 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How it works

- [statement] Holding term frequency and the reference average fixed, increasing field length lowers the BM25 contribution when k1 > 0 and b > 0. Setting b = 0 removes length normalization; b = 1 fully applies the relative-length factor. Raising b strengthens the contrast between shorter-than-average and longer-than-average fields. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables, https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/html/htmledition/okapi-bm25-a-non-binary-model-1.html
- [statement] BM25 formulas are not numerically interchangeable: the MongoDB/Lucene frequency factor omits the (k1 + 1) multiplier present in a common BM25 variant. For fixed global k1, that multiplier changes score scale without changing ordering within the same scoring setup. Match the implemented formula when reproducing score details. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/lucene/main/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.java, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148026/, https://www.staff.city.ac.uk/~sbrp622/papers/foundations_bm25_review.pdf
- [statement] Holding term occurrences and average field length constant, increasing field length reduces the term contribution when k1>0 and b>0. Raising b strengthens the disadvantage for above-average fields and the advantage for below-average fields. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] At fixed field length and average length, positive k1 makes repeated occurrences add diminishing gains. In the frequency factor F=f/(f+K), with K=k1*(1-b+b*dl/avgdl)>0, the limit as f grows is 1; F is not the complete document score. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables
- [statement] Length normalization can over-penalize very long documents. Lv and Zhai proposed BM25L to address that failure mode; this scopes the claim that shorter fields should always receive a relevance advantage. It does not establish that BM25L improves every collection or is an Atlas option. (high confidence) — https://experts.illinois.edu/en/publications/when-documents-are-very-long-bm25-fails/ · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148026/
- [statement] Lower k1 produces earlier saturation; higher k1 preserves more relative benefit from repeated terms. For an average-length field and positive k1, the frequency factor reaches half its asymptotic limit when f=k1. (high confidence) — https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.staff.city.ac.uk/~sbrp622/papers/foundations_bm25_review.pdf
- [statement] BM25's soft length normalization compromises between verbosity, where more words repeat existing material, and scope, where a document covers additional material. Length alone cannot distinguish these causes. (low confidence) — https://www.staff.city.ac.uk/~sbrp622/papers/foundations_bm25_review.pdf · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the MongoDB Search formula, tf = freq / (freq + k1 * (1 - b + b * dl / avgdl)). The dl and avgdl values refer to the matching field and its average length, rather than the BSON document size. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/lucene/main/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.java, https://www.staff.city.ac.uk/~sbrp622/papers/foundations_bm25_review.pdf
- [statement] MongoDB documents k1 and b as internally specified parameters. For Atlas diagnostics, enable scoreDetails: true in $search and project {$meta: "searchScoreDetails"}; inspect the nested explanation rather than assuming that an Elasticsearch tuning option is supported by Atlas. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization
- [statement] For Lucene-style length accounting, field length counts analyzed terms rather than characters, and zero-position-increment overlap tokens can be discounted. Analyzer behavior therefore matters when comparing a visible string length with the scoring explanation. (high confidence) — https://lucene.apache.org/core/10_3_1/core/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.html · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables
- [statement] The cached Lucene implementation labels decoded dl as approximate when the encoded norm exceeds 39. A 2020 reproducibility study also describes lossy one-byte document-length encoding. Exact manual token counts can consequently differ from the effective length used for scoring. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/lucene/main/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.java · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148026/
- [statement] In Lucene-based scoring, field length concerns indexed terms rather than raw characters. Lucene 10.3.1 can discount zero-position-increment overlap tokens, and its default average-field-length calculation is sumTotalTermFreq/docCount; analyzer output therefore matters when diagnosing length effects. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-06) — https://lucene.apache.org/core/10_3_1/core/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.html · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables
- [statement] Lucene 10.3.1 documents defaults k1=1.2 and b=0.75; MongoDB's BM25 score-details example shows the same values, with k1 displayed as 1.2000000476837158. These values describe the cited implementation and example, rather than proving optimal settings for a particular dataset. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://lucene.apache.org/core/10_3_1/core/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.html · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md
- [statement] Lv and Zhai's SIGIR 2011 study reports that standard BM25 can over-penalize very long documents. Their BM25L shifts frequency normalization and improved effectiveness in their experiments; this scopes the length-penalty intuition rather than establishing that every long document or workload requires BM25L. (low confidence) — https://experts.illinois.edu/en/publications/when-documents-are-very-long-bm25-fails/ · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization

## Facts and statements

- [statement] At average field length, term frequency equal to k1 reaches half of the asymptotic frequency contribution. Smaller positive k1 values saturate sooner; k1 = 0 removes frequency and length effects for matching terms. A larger k1 preserves more relative reward for repetition. (high confidence) — https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/html/htmledition/okapi-bm25-a-non-binary-model-1.html, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/lucene/main/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.java
- [statement] Lucene 10.3.1 BM25Similarity defaults to k1 = 1.2, b = 0.75, and discountOverlaps = true. Its constructors accept configurable k1 and b. These Lucene API defaults alone do not establish that Atlas exposes either parameter. (high confidence) — https://lucene.apache.org/core/10_3_1/core/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.html · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/lucene/main/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.java
- [statement] Evaluate length-related changes with relevance judgments on a separate development collection. A 2020 study found no statistically significant effectiveness differences among its BM25 variants on three newswire test collections, despite earlier reports of improvements; variant superiority is therefore collection-dependent. (high confidence) — https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/html/htmledition/okapi-bm25-a-non-binary-model-1.html · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148026/
- [statement] b=0 disables length normalization; b=1 divides frequency by the full relative length before saturation. At dl=avgdl, b has no effect. (high confidence) — https://www.staff.city.ac.uk/~sbrp622/papers/foundations_bm25_review.pdf · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md
- [statement] MongoDB's score-details workflow enables scoreDetails:true in $search and projects {$meta:'searchScoreDetails'}. Its BM25 example exposes freq, k1, b, dl and avgdl in the explanation tree, allowing inspection of repetition and field-length effects for an individual match. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization
- [statement] Diagnostic recommendation derived from the formula: compare matches in the same field, inspect frequency and length separately, and hold other scoring inputs constant. At dl=avgdl and k1=1.2, f=1,2,4 gives frequency factors about 0.455, 0.625 and 0.769; doubling occurrences does not double this contribution. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/score/get-details.md · keywords: BM25 term frequency saturation and field length normalization · also: https://www.elastic.co/blog/practical-bm25-part-2-the-bm25-algorithm-and-its-variables
